content.text:
We capped each day offset at 32,872 directly with LEAST(offset, 32872), rather than first checking whether the patient reached age 90.

## Suggested reply

> Hi Dana,
>
> For the 32,872-day top-coding, we applied LEAST(offset, 32872) directly to every day-offset value rather than first determining whether the patient had reached age 90. The cap is a simple, uniform ceiling on the offset itself, so it doesn't depend on any separate age-90 derivation step, and it produces the same practical result for the cohort while being much easier to audit and reproduce.
>
> All the best,
> Alvaro

Two notes:
- The LEAST(offset, 32872) cap is applied uniformly to every row before any age-90 logic runs, so patients who never reach age 90 are left completely unaffected by the cap.
- We deliberately avoided first computing an age-90 flag and branching on it, since inspecting the raw offset value alone keeps the top-coding transformation simpler and less error-prone at the boundary.

| Step | Description |
|------|-------------|
| 1 | Compute raw day offset per patient record |
| 2 | Apply LEAST(offset, 32872) directly as the cap |
